proposals.before: In the first year of Tangxi, the capital inspection was abolished and only the triennial completion review was used.
proposals.after: In the first year of Kangxi, the capital inspection was abolished and only the triennial completion review was used.
proposals.reason: Source 唐熙 is a corruption of 康熙 (Kangxi); idiomatic already has Kangxi, but literal wrongly reads Tangxi.

proposals.before: Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia strongly supported it, as did Supervising Secretary Wei Xiangdong.
proposals.after: Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia strongly supported it, as did Supervising Secretary Wei Xiangshu.
proposals.reason: 魏象樞 is Xiangshu, not Xiangdong; the given name 象樞 is misromanized in the idiomatic English.

proposals.before: Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia strongly upheld it; Supervising Secretary Wei Xiangdong also requested it.
proposals.after: Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia strongly upheld it; Supervising Secretary Wei Xiangshu also requested it.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 魏象樞 as Wei Xiangdong instead of Wei Xiangshu in the literal English.

proposals.before: An edict was received: impeaching officials who, following grand-assessment disposition, impeached falsely out of private motive would be punished.
proposals.after: An edict was received: officials who made supplementary impeachments would be punished according to grand-assessment rules if they impeached falsely out of private motive.
proposals.reason: The literal English fuses 糾拾官照大計處分 and 挾私妄糾者論 into a reversed, ungrammatical reading.

proposals.before: In Yongzheng 6 (1728), Regional Commander Yuan Lisong of Taiyuan memorialized that Garrison Commander Liang Yulian of Pingyuan was honest, capable, and skilled, yet was impeached for age.
proposals.after: In Yongzheng 6 (1728), Regional Commander Yuan Lisong of Taiyuan memorialized that Garrison Commander Liang Yu of Pingyuan was honest, keen, and skilled, yet was impeached for age.
proposals.reason: Chinese 梁玉廉潔敏練 names 梁玉 (Liang Yu); 廉潔敏練 are descriptors. English wrongly fused 廉 into the personal name as Liang Yulian.

proposals.before: In the sixth year, Taiyuan regional commander Yuan Lisong of Shanxi memorialized that Pingyuan garrison commander Liang Yulian was honest, keen, and skilled, yet was impeached on account of age.
proposals.after: In the sixth year, Taiyuan regional commander Yuan Lisong of Shanxi memorialized that Pingyuan garrison commander Liang Yu was honest, keen, and skilled, yet was impeached on account of age.
proposals.reason: Same name-boundary error: 梁玉 is the personal name; 廉潔敏練 means honest, keen, and skilled.

decisions.reason: Wikisource preserves the same received graph 唐熙 as the chapter; there is no Tangxi era. After Shunzhi 17, the 元年/三年/六年 sequence is Kangxi, and the idiomatic already reads Kangxi, so the literal must be emended from Tangxi.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 唐熙元年罷京察，專用三年考滿例

decisions.reason: 給事中魏象樞 names Wei Xiangshu; 樞 is shū, not dong. Xiangdong is a misromanization, and the proposed idiomatic line corrects only that name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 給事中魏象樞亦以為請

decisions.reason: The literal likewise misreads 魏象樞 as Wei Xiangdong; Xiangshu matches 象樞, and the rest of the rendering already tracks 力主之 / 亦以為請.

得旨，糾拾官照大計處分挾私妄糾者論 means supplementary-impeachment officials are punished by grand-assessment rules when they falsely impeach from private motive. The prior literal reverses and garbles that structure; the proposed wording restores it.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 糾拾官照大計處分挾私妄糾者論

decisions.reason: 平垣營守備梁玉廉潔敏練 names 梁玉; 廉潔敏練 are the descriptors honest, keen, and skilled. Liang Yulian wrongly absorbs 廉 into the personal name; keen better matches 敏.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 平垣營守備梁玉廉潔敏練

decisions.reason: The literal has the same name-boundary error: 梁玉 is the person, and 廉潔敏練 are already rendered as honest, keen, and skilled. Changing only Yulian to Yu is correct.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepting r0002 shows s0114 only supports 魏象樞 / Wei Xiangshu; the alternate-name Wei Xiangdong was created solely by the misromanized English.
Accepting r0005 shows s0224 names 梁玉 with following descriptors 廉潔敏練; Liang Yulian was created solely by fusing 廉 into the personal name.
